title: How many calls are open at once?
hook: A function calls itself. Does the new call replace the old one, or wait on top of it?

knows: calling a function and getting a value back
doesNotKnow: that each unfinished call waits with its own copy of its variables
why a recursive function needs a base case

misconception: A recursive call replaces the earlier one, so only one call exists at a time.
objective: The learner can explain that factorial(3) has 4 calls open at its deepest moment (for 3, 2, 1 and 0), each with its own n and waiting for the one above, and that the base case factorial(0) = 1 lets the answers 1, 1, 2, 6 return back up.

claims.text: At the deepest moment of factorial(3), 4 calls are open: factorial(3), factorial(2), factorial(1) and factorial(0).
claims.source: Builder instrumented a depth counter around a recursive factorial in Node: max depth 4. Demo.tsx MAX_DEPTH = TOP + 1.

claims.text: A new call does not replace the old one: each call keeps its own n and waits for the call it made.
claims.source: Activation records / stack frames: Patterson and Hennessy, Computer Organization and Design, 2.8 'Supporting Procedures in Computer Hardware' (procedure frames on the stack; recursive fact example).

claims.text: The answers come back as 1, 1, 2, 6: factorial(0) = 1, factorial(1) = 1 × 1, factorial(2) = 2 × 1, factorial(3) = 3 × 2.
claims.source: Builder logged return values in Node: ret 0 → 1, 1 → 1, 2 → 2, 3 → 6. Demo.tsx fact().

claims.text: factorial(0) = 1 is the base case: the one call that answers without calling again.
claims.source: Definition given in the question; 0! = 1 by convention (empty product).

claims.text: Without a base case the calls never stop, the stack runs out of room and the program crashes with a stack overflow.
claims.source: Builder ran const g = n => n * g(n - 1); g(3) in Node 22: RangeError 'Maximum call stack size exceeded'.

recall.question: sum(n) = n + sum(n − 1), with sum(0) = 0. While sum(0) is running inside sum(5), how many calls of sum are open?
recall.why: Each call waits for the one it made, so sum(5), sum(4), sum(3), sum(2), sum(1) and sum(0) are all open: 6.
